summary.headline: TI standalone Q2 FY27 revenue rose to Rs.2,710 Cr (from Rs.2,119 Cr) but PBT was flat at Rs.253 Cr as raw-material pass-through lagged.
summary.overview: Standalone revenue grew about 28% YoY to Rs.2,710 Cr, with management attributing roughly 15% to volume and the rest to raw-material price pass-through. Standalone PBT was nearly flat at Rs.253 Cr versus Rs.250 Cr, and EBITDA was flat per an analyst, as commodity and cell-cost increases reached margins before customer price recovery. Consolidated revenue rose to Rs.7,330 Cr from Rs.5,523 Cr, driven by CG Power, while TICMPL (EV) revenue reached Rs.476 Cr and remained loss-making. Management expects price recovery to settle over one to two quarters and reiterated TICMPL EBITDA breakeven targets for truck in Q4 FY27.

segments.name: Engineering division
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs.1,828 Cr (vs Rs.1,382 Cr) with PBIT Rs.171 Cr (vs Rs.164 Cr). Includes Metal Formed Products at Rs.473 Cr revenue (vs Rs.408 Cr) and PBIT Rs.49 Cr (vs Rs.44 Cr).

segments.commentary: Revenue Rs.247 Cr (vs Rs.194 Cr) with PBIT Rs.8 Cr (vs Rs.4 Cr).

segments.commentary: Revenue Rs.260 Cr (vs Rs.227 Cr) with PBIT Rs.20 Cr (vs Rs.18 Cr).

segments.commentary: Revenue Rs.3,802 Cr (vs Rs.2,923 Cr) and PBT Rs.559 Cr (vs Rs.388 Cr).

segments.commentary: Revenue Rs.128 Cr (vs Rs.132 Cr) and PBT Rs.20 Cr (vs Rs.29 Cr).

segments.name: TICMPL (EV, Clean Mobility)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs.476 Cr in Q2, with H1 revenue exceeding full FY26 revenue; cash about Rs.350 Cr; Rs.250 Cr CCPS infusion from TI in the quarter. Segment costs rose sharply on cell prices, rupee and commodities.

guidance_outlook: Price pass-through on commodity increases expected to fully recover in one to two quarters; management said it expects EBITDA to catch up in H2 FY27 and FY28 in absolute terms.

TICMPL: truck business targeted for EBITDA breakeven in Q4 FY27; two more businesses targeted for EBITDA breakeven in Q4 FY28; then PAT profitability. Company-level revenue guidance not given, but every quarter targeted to beat the previous one.
Management reiterated aspiration of USD 1 billion revenue for TICMPL by 2030, at consolidated TICMPL level.
Medium-term medical business profitability expected at higher double-digit levels.
CDMO: regulatory approvals expected to take about a year; commercial supplies to begin about a quarter earlier; meaningful revenue growth expected in about a year.
Cash flow target of about 85% FCF to PAT internally, excluding subsidiary investments; a higher capex year may cause deviation.
TICMPL cash of about Rs.350 Cr considered sufficient for FY27; funding need for FY28 to be revisited by Q4.
risks_watch: Pass-through lag: standalone EBITDA flat YoY despite about 15% volume growth; recovery timing has slipped before and must be confirmed in Q3 FY27.
TICMPL losses continue (about Rs.150 Cr referenced by analyst) with cell price, rupee and commodity headwinds; breakeven timelines have slipped historically.
Competition rising from Chinese and new Indian e-truck entrants; passenger e-3W share only low single digits.
CCPS terms changed; investor stakes in TICMPL remain contingent on exit valuation, though management says accounting and returns are unchanged.
Capital allocation: large cash build and subsidiary investments; FCF to PAT target 85% excludes subsidiary investments.
Export share stuck near 15% against an earlier 20% target.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term EV and medical targets and on full margin recovery, but noticeably vague on timing and numbers: segment price-volume split deferred to next quarter, TICMPL revenue outlook declined, and the CCPS terms and electronics acquisition left open.
key_quotes: So, at a TI level, approximately, you can consider about 15% there is a volume growth, and rest is coming on account of the raw material price increases.
We are definitely targeting at least one business, which is our truck business, to be an EBITDA breakeven in Q4 this year
So, if you were to ask my personal opinion, I am not happy with any of the four numbers.

qa_highlights.question: How much of standalone growth is volume versus HRC/raw-material pass-through, and why are engineering and MFP margins below expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 15% is volume and the rest is raw-material price increases. Margin pressure is from a lag of one to two quarters in settling prices with customers and OEMs, which comes with retrospective effect; full recovery is expected in the next one or two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Will standalone EBITDA catch up in H2 FY27 given flat EBITDA on 15-16% volume growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management answered '100% yes' that absolute profit lost in H1 will be caught up in H2 FY27 and FY28, with profitability returning to earlier levels after recovery.

qa_highlights.question: What is the TICMPL outlook on revenue and breakeven, and how much more funding is needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Jalaj Gupta declined to give revenue projections beyond aiming for each quarter to beat the last; truck business targeted for EBITDA breakeven in Q4 FY27 and two more in Q4 FY28, then PAT. AN Meyyappan said cash of about Rs.350 Cr covers FY27, with FY28 needs to be revisited by Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Did the Rs.250 Cr CCPS infusion include proportionate investment from external partners, and are CCPS terms changed?
qa_highlights.answer: AN Meyyappan said external investors have not put in any money since their Rs.2,250 Cr; the Rs.250 Cr came only from TI. On CCPS, he said accounting and returns are unchanged, but stakes depend on exit valuation and are not yet fixed.

qa_highlights.question: How does management view competition and its moat in EV, and what are the market shares?
qa_highlights.answer: Jalaj Gupta said competition is rising but the group entered all four segments early; moat rests on learning curve (over 1,000 SCVs and 300 tractors on road), supplier and dealer relationships, electric-only focus and indigenous-design subsidies. Trucks hold about 25-26% share against 11-12 players, aiming for top three in all four segments.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capital allocation plan given expected capex, subsidiary investments and cash build?
qa_highlights.answer: Mukesh Ahuja said the internal FCF-to-PAT target is about 85%, excluding subsidiary investments, with a higher-capex year as a permitted deviation. Cash from TI and CG Power will fund newer businesses (medical, CDMO, MIM acquisition) and possible adjacencies in the core business, with nothing finalised.

capex_capacity: Standalone capex over next two years was asked but not quantified; management only reiterated cash-flow guideline of about 85% FCF to PAT internally, excluding subsidiary investments, with a higher-capex year allowed to deviate
TICMPL: H1 revenue exceeded full FY26 revenue; cash about Rs.350 Cr considered sufficient for FY27 with no fundraise needed; FY28 funding to be revisited by Q4 FY27

TICMPL: Rs.250 Cr CCPS infusion in Q2 came entirely from TI; external investors had put in Rs.2,250 Cr earlier and added nothing since; Rs.78 Cr invested in Shanthi Gears; total subsidiary infusion Rs.412 Cr

CDMO: semi-commercial plant commissioned and quantities supplied to a customer; clean room commissioned, validation batches in intermediate block nearing completion, moving to clean room in 3-4 weeks; regulatory approvals expected to take about a year, commercial supplies about a quarter earlier

Medical: plastic medical devices (IV cannula, canister) business acquired as a small startup; sales team and manpower to be in place by end of Q3 FY27; further facility investment to follow capacity utilisation of current facility
demand_pricing: Standalone revenue growth of about 28% YoY split as roughly 15% volume and the rest raw-material price pass-through; segment-wise price-volume split deferred to next quarter or two
Pass-through: contracts with customers and OEMs reset with retrospective effect; settlement takes one to two quarters, management confident of full recovery within that window
EV volumes Q2 FY27 vs Q1 FY27: trucks 311 vs 86; three-wheelers 2,242 vs 1,924; small commercial vehicles 483 vs 347; electric tractors 50 vs 22

EV market share: about 25-26% in trucks (market of 11-12 players) and SCV; about 25% of tractor VAHAN registrations in H1; low single digit in passenger e-3W; low single digit but rising in cargo e-3W (Super Auto) at about 200 units per month

TICMPL cost pressure in Q2 from cell prices, adverse rupee and commodities; mitigation via price correction, deal-by-deal realisation improvement and BOM cost reduction; medical business growing 20%+ per management
Exports stuck at about 15% of TI revenue versus earlier 20% target, all exports from the engineering division and other businesses; competition from Chinese and new Indian e-truck entrants

growth.why: Management guides to EBITDA catch-up in H2 FY27 and FY28 and every quarter beating the last, backed by ~15% volume growth, EV volume gains (trucks 311 vs 86 QoQ) and CDMO/medical launches, but no quantified capacity or order book and standalone capex was not quantified; TICMPL truck EBITDA breakeven targeted Q4 FY27.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management said 100% yes that H1 lost absolute profit (standalone PBT flat at Rs.253 Cr vs Rs.250 Cr on ~15% volume growth) will be caught up in H2 FY27 and FY28, as 1-2 quarter raw-material pass-through lag settles, though segment price-volume split was deferred.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: CDMO clean room commissioned with validation batches moving to clean room in 3-4 weeks and semi-commercial plant already commissioned, but capacity size not quantified and medical facility investment only follows utilisation of current facility.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Standalone revenue grew ~28% with ~15% from volume; EV volumes rose QoQ (trucks 311 vs 86, 3W 2,242 vs 1,924, SCV 483 vs 347), and management aims for every quarter to beat the previous one, though no quantified volume guide was given.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Standalone capex over two years was not quantified and a higher-capex year is an allowed deviation from the 85% FCF-to-PAT target; TICMPL FY28 funding is to be revisited by Q4 FY27 with Rs.350 Cr cash covering FY27, so no firm announcement yet.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No company-level revenue guidance was given and TICMPL revenue outlook was declined, so there is no basis for an upgrade in the window; only qualitative 'beat last quarter' language.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Pass-through recovery must be confirmed in Q3 FY27 after slipping before, and TICMPL losses (about Rs.150 Cr cited by analyst) with cell, rupee and commodity headwinds plus historically slipping breakeven timelines add risk.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: CDMO commercial supplies to start about a quarter earlier than the ~1-year approval timeline, and medical plastic devices (IV cannula, canister) sales team to be in place by end of Q3 FY27; TICMPL truck EBITDA breakeven targeted Q4 FY27.

rows.label: TICMPL truck EBITDA breakeven
rows.why: Management targets truck business EBITDA breakeven in Q4 FY27 on 311 truck units in Q2 vs 86 in Q1 and ~25-26% share, though breakeven timelines have slipped historically.

rows.label: TICMPL FY28 funding review
rows.why: Rs.350 Cr cash considered sufficient for FY27 with no fundraise needed, and FY28 funding is to be revisited by Q4 FY27, after a Rs.250 Cr CCPS infusion from TI alone in Q2.

rows.label: Export share recovery
rows.why: Exports are stuck at about 15% of TI revenue against an earlier 20% target, with competition from Chinese and new Indian e-truck entrants.

tone.note: Management was confident on full margin recovery in H2 FY27 and long-term EV and medical targets, but vague on timing and numbers (segment price-volume split deferred, TICMPL revenue outlook declined, CCPS terms open); analysts pushed on flat standalone EBITDA, TICMPL losses and funding.
